description.value: In this assessment, students address the environmental and economic impacts of the 'Throw Away Society' by constructing a durable, long-term storage solution and designing a sustainable iteration. The task requires students to apply technical skills to manufacture a pencil box according to specific design requirements, demonstrating the safe and effective use of appropriate technologies and processes. Concurrently, students use the SBC Year 7 Design Model to develop an improved version of the product that incorporates principles of the Circular Economy. Through a folio of work, students document their design process, justifying their selection of materials and components while communicating innovative ideas through sophisticated design drawings. The final folio evaluates how design modifications can enhance sustainability and product longevity within a modern context.
description.aiNotes:
The quest for new and innovative products combined with profits being made by companies selling as many units as possible has resulted in what is termed a Throw Away Society, where increasingly the cost of repair is more than the cost of replacement. The resultant drain on landfill, construction resources and associated carbon emissions all point to the unsustainability of a Throw Away Society. 

In this unit students will acquire the skills to build and maintain a key item required for the completion of their secondary and tertiary studies as well as produce an improved design that will add to the sustainability and associated financial savings of a pencil box that will last for multiple decades.

Your task is to create a pencil case to the specifications of the design attached, using the materials provided. 

You are also required to design an improved version of the pencil case you have made, incorporating elements of sustainability and the Circular Economy. This design task will be completed as a folio of work, documenting the use of the SBC year 7 Design Model, resulting in a final design drawing.

Assessment Objectives:
•	Develop, modify and communicate design ideas by applying creativity, innovation and skills of increasing sophistication.
•	Work flexibly to effectively and safely test, select, justify and use appropriate technologies and processes to make designed solutions.

conditions.value:
• Construction: Completed in a supervised workshop environment adhering to Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) protocols.
• Design Folio: 4–6 A3 pages (or digital equivalent) documenting the application of the SBC Year 7 Design Model.
• Evidence: A physical prototype constructed to specifications and a folio containing annotated graphical representations, justification of material and process selections, and a final design drawing.

conditionsOther.value:
• 6–8 weeks of class time
• Folio: 4–6 A3 pages or equivalent digital media pages, including annotated design drawings and justification of material/component selection
• Supervised conditions: Manufacturing of the physical prototype must be completed in the college workshop under teacher supervision
• Safety: Students must successfully complete mandatory workshop safety inductions and tool-specific competency tests prior to manufacturing
• Drafting: Monitoring of the design folio at Week 5 and conferencing of the final evaluation in Week 9
• Internal moderation: Departmental moderation conferencing to ensure consistency of teacher judgment against achievement standards

resourcesAvailable.value: Workshop, project drawing, folio template and exemplar response.
